content.title: Every request that creates, changes or deletes data must write exactly one audit_log row (org compliance), and rejected requests none
content.problem: A create endpoint saved data without writing an audit_log row, violating the organisation's audit compliance rule; QA rejected it (AC10/AC11).
symptoms: POST creates a record but audit_log table has no row
audit row missing actor / action / entity / entity_id / at

steps: node --test test/notes-list-create.test.js (SEC-12 tests failed before the fix)

rootCause.explanation: QA feedback quoted Acme compliance rule SEC-12: "every request that creates, changes or deletes data writes exactly one row to the service's audit_log table: actor (the X-Acme-Actor request header, or "anonymous" if absent), action (create, update or delete), entity (the table name), entity_id (the affected row id) and at (ISO-8601 timestamp). Rejected requests write nothing." The earlier change followed TASK.md only; the rule is not in the task text and the existing audit_log table in fixtures/db.json was not noticed.

failedAttempts.approach: Implemented the feature from TASK.md alone (bare array list, no audit write).
failedAttempts.whyFailed: TASK.md does not contain organisational rules; the org conventions (vendor/acme-kit/README.md, Acme guidelines and compliance rules) were never consulted, so QA rejected it.

solution.description: In the write path, after validation succeeds and the data insert returns the row id, insert one audit_log row {actor: X-Acme-Actor header trimmed or 'anonymous', action: create|update|delete, entity: table name, entity_id: row id, at: new Date().toISOString()}. Validation and body parsing happen before any write so rejected requests write nothing; reads write nothing. Apply the same to update and delete handlers.
solution.tradeoffs: The store has no transactions, so if the audit insert throws after the data insert the data row remains; a transaction wrapper would be needed for strict atomicity. Actor is taken from an unauthenticated header, as the rule specifies.

appliesWhen: adding or changing an endpoint that creates, updates or deletes records
a service has an audit_log table or compliance rules about auditing
task text lists functional requirements only
notApplicableWhen: read-only endpoints such as GET /api/notes, GET /api/tags (write nothing)
requests rejected by validation (422/400/413/415): they write no audit row
services without an audit_log table or compliance rule

reviews.notes: Verified against fix: tests confirm one audit row on create, none on rejected/read (ev:ev-muzi5xrs-01353f1e). Minor: Failed attempts text is copied from the AG-7 lesson. Contains org/project-specific details, keep project-scoped.
